subject: forge-norvialabs
title: Kernel confinement is the boundary, not approvals: shell is deliberately NOT HITL-gated, and on a host that cannot confine (no bwrap, nested-sandbox sandbox_apply failure) the CLI refuses to start rather than running unconfined
evidence: crates/forge-tools/src/sandbox.rs:1-37 (decision/enforcement planes split by dependency graph; scope 'matching Codex's workspace-write', .git/.forge read-only so a confined process cannot widen its own permissions), :342-361 (availability), :369-381 (cached sandbox_apply probe), :389-393 (bwrap/socat by absolute path only, so agent-influenced PATH cannot move the boundary); crates/forge-governance/src/lib.rs:47-50 (shell not gated because CLI won't start unconfined); SECURITY.md threat-model section
one_why: The inverse default of the whole corpus: nanocoder jails opt-in, tura gates by regex denylist, forge gates nothing textual and removes the unconfined code path entirely -- the honest register ('the approval prompt is a second, weaker layer') is the cheapest half to port.

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: Per-session deny-by-default egress proxy: nothing pre-allowed (crates.io/npmjs/pypi/github asserted 403 in tests), only PERSONAL permissions.toml host rules open it -- repo-committed allows never do; denied hosts escalate as typed approval kinds with host_grant_stays_filesystem_sandboxed
evidence: crates/forge-core/src/permission.rs:36-48 (repo allows never loosen), :61-84 (proxy start, socket outside workspace, failure leaves network off), :143-167 (refuses former ecosystem hosts), :308-330 (only personal allows open), :470-511 (subagent inherits parent grant, never a second proxy); crates/forge-cli/src/main.rs:205-221 (denied_host / sandbox_escalation / governance_approval JSON kinds); socat relay into the bwrap netns at crates/forge-tools/src/sandbox.rs:404-420
one_why: Same direction as codex's separate network approval but with a sharper trust split: a poisoned repo cannot widen its own network policy, and proxy-start failure degrades to offline rather than to open network -- the three failure modes are each pinned by a test.

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: Protected-facts gate inside a fully transactional compaction: user-authored constraints/corrections/decisions/irreversible-actions are extracted from canonical history, fed to the checkpoint prompt as must-keep, and the candidate is REJECTED (MissingProtectedFacts) before install; compaction commits-or-rolls-back with a new cache epoch
evidence: crates/forge-context/src/compaction/facts.rs:1-40; crates/forge-context/src/compaction/engine.rs:1-5,35-47 (pure proposal, never mutates; NotSmaller/StillOversized/InvalidStructure/MissingProtectedFacts); crates/forge-core/src/session/compaction.rs:7-18 (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK), :282-311 (install journals + opens cache epoch); crates/forge-context/src/compaction/policy.rs:105-106 (trigger includes next-turn projection so it fires before overflow)
one_why: Same survival-gate idea grinta found, but wired as a hard install precondition with deliberately shallow extraction (user text only, no intent classifier) and paired with the runway gate that refuses compactions too small to pay for breaking the cached prefix.

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: Permission model tested as a behavior contract: permission_contract.rs spawns real processes and asserts what the kernel did, written around four historical defects a unit test missed (inert rule from /var vs /private/var, --tmpfs symlink abort, bind/mask ordering, cross-layer gap); sandbox_is_available_on_linux_in_ci fails the build if CI loses bubblewrap so skips can't silently untest the suite
evidence: crates/forge-tools/tests/permission_contract.rs:1-40 (design comment + three properties), :104-127 (Expect::Denied rows); crates/forge-tools/tests/sandbox_enforcement.rs:1-47,1177; .github/workflows/ci.yml:24-35 (apt-get bubblewrap socat 'worth spending an apt-get on', installer tested)
one_why: The anti-silent-skip machinery is the portable part: loud skip reasons locally, a test that asserts the CI runner can confine, and a table someone can scan to see exactly what the sandbox promises.

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: Cache epochs as first-state: a cache_epoch counter bumped on compaction/transport change, journal-restored; prompt-wire snapshots diff common prefixes and log CACHE PREFIX INVALIDATED naming the diverging part -- gated off the production hot path unless DEBUG; cross-provider usage normalization so Anthropic's uncached-only vs OpenAI's total prompt_tokens mean one quantity
one_why: Below smelt's fuzzed cache-invariance and pi's warming, but the epoch model makes every cache invalidation an attributable event (reason + journal entry) instead of a hope, and the usage-semantics normalization fixes hit-rate math every cross-provider harness silently gets wrong.

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: MCP schema deferral is budget-gated against the SAME window arithmetic as compaction: full schemas are sent until they exceed 10% of usable context (tool_schema_budget), then replaced by a SearchToolsTool catalog
one_why: Maki's deferred-catalog idea, with the missing bit maki lacks: an explicit, tested token budget tied to the real usable window so the switch is arithmetic, not a setting.

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: SQLite event journal replays EXECUTION state, not just messages: queue items, background tasks, pending HITL, composer lines, cache epoch, compaction count, plus tool-intent-before-execution with incomplete_intents for crash reconciliation
evidence: crates/forge-durable/src/lib.rs:85-138 (ReplayState fields), :469 (append_tool_intent), :92 (incomplete_intents); crates/forge-durable/tests/replay_perf.rs; crates/forge-core/src/turn.rs:24-29 (Failed-lifecycle re-entry prevents wedged resume)
one_why: Most journals replay the transcript and rebuild the rest loosely; forge's replay state is the full supervisor snapshot, which is what makes resume-and-keep-going (including an in-flight approval) possible.

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: Supervisor goal-loop: a completion condition is judged by a separate one-line-verdict evaluator (MET/NOT_MET/IMPOSSIBLE, strict parse, condition wrapped as untrusted, 'do not accept an assistant claim as proof'), auto-continuing the session up to MAX_GOAL_TURNS=30
one_why: Octomind's independent-verifier shape applied to autonomous continuation rather than a finish declaration; the cap and the one-line parse contract keep the judge itself from becoming the loop.

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: Agent Skills open standard (agentskills.io) implemented as discovery/activation/execution stages: only name+description in the system prompt, SKILL.md and bundled reference/script files fetched on demand through a load_skill tool
evidence: crates/forge-tools/src/skills.rs:1-35 (stage docs + LoadSkillArgs); discovery in forge-core assemble_system_prompt via forge_context::discover_skills
one_why: Convergence data point on the seeded id: this one keys to the published open standard rather than a project-proprietary format, and ties bundled-file access to the skill's own directory.
